event_questions.label: E1
event_questions.not_this: No: only a file stating that no notice of termination has been given at all (also a lease of limited duration that simply ends on its agreed date, a termination only announced or threatened, a notice given by the tenant). A notice the landlord says was sent and the tenant says never reached him is open, not no.
event_questions.question: Has the landlord given the tenant notice terminating the lease of the dwelling, and has it reached the tenant?

event_questions.label: E2
event_questions.not_this: A landlord's plan to raise the rent that has not been announced, demanded or charged; the initial rent agreed for a new lease; new accessory charges or reduced services without a higher rent.
event_questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord has announced, demanded or charged a higher rent for the dwelling, by a notice, a letter, an invoice or otherwise (whether or not on an official form)?

questions.label: Q1
questions.not_this: A landlord who learned of the defect from the caretaker, the property manager or an inspection, although the tenant never wrote: that landlord knows, so the answer is no.
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord does not yet know of the defect (the tenant has not reported it and the landlord has not learned of it in another way)?

questions.label: Q2
questions.not_this: A defect the claim itself attributes wholly to the tenant, or says he must remedy at his own expense, is no. A cause the claim calls shared or disputed is open, not no; a landlord's allegation that the tenant caused it, which the claim disputes, does not make this no.
questions.question: Does the claim state that the rented dwelling has a defect (for example mould, damp, or heating that fails) or that the tenant is disturbed in using the dwelling as agreed, without the claim itself saying that the tenant alone caused the defect or must remedy it at his own expense?

questions.label: Q3
questions.not_this: A deposit that is announced or planned but not yet made; the rental security paid at the start of the lease.
questions.question: Does the claim state that at least one rent payment has already been paid into deposit with the office designated by the canton?

questions.label: Q4
questions.not_this: Withholding or reducing the rent without paying it to a deposit office; the rental security paid at the start of the lease.
questions.question: Does the claim state that the tenant intends to pay the rent on deposit with the office designated by the canton instead of to the landlord, or has begun to do so?

questions.label: Q5
questions.not_this: A reduction of the rent for the reduced use of the dwelling (art. 259d), which is not compensation for damage.
questions.question: Does the tenant claim compensation from the landlord for damage the defect caused to the tenant (for example damaged furniture or clothing, or extra costs)?

questions.label: Q6
questions.not_this: A tenant who told the landlord by telephone and later confirmed it by letter, e-mail or text message: a written trace exists, so the answer is no.
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord learned of the defect only orally, so that no written notice, written acknowledgement or inspection record of it exists?

routing.question: Which tenancy dispute does the claim concern: a defect of the dwelling or a disturbance of its agreed use that the tenant did not cause (for example mould, damp, or heating that fails), a termination of the lease by the landlord, or a rent increase? A rent increase that the landlord accompanied with a notice of termination is a rent increase dispute: the rent-increase rules examine that notice (art. 269d para. 2 let. c).

text:
Grüezi

Ich wohne seit April 2024 in einer 3-Zimmer-Wohnung der Moosacker Handels AG am Sonnenweg 4 in Wohlen und zahle CHF 1740 im Monat. Ich möchte vorausschicken, dass ich mit der Wohnung an sich sehr zufrieden bin. Es ist nichts kaputt, es gibt keinen Schimmel, keinen Lärm, die Heizung läuft, und nichts hindert mich daran, so zu wohnen, wie es abgemacht ist. Darum geht es also nicht.

Mein Problem ist ein anderes. Ich habe von meiner Firma das Angebot bekommen, von September bis Ende Februar in unserer Niederlassung in Lyon zu arbeiten. Danach komme ich sicher zurück. In dieser Zeit möchte ich das Gästezimmer und auch die übrige Wohnung an meine langjährige Freundin Corinne Odermatt untervermieten, zum gleichen Preis, den ich selbst bezahle. Ich habe das Herrn Oliver Hürlimann von der Verwaltung schon im Mai mündlich angekündigt und am 16. Juni schriftlich mit allen Angaben beantragt.

Am 6. Juli kam seine Antwort: Untervermietung komme bei der Moosacker grundsätzlich nicht in Frage, ich solle die Wohnung halt kündigen, wenn ich weg sei. Eine Begründung gibt er nicht. Ich will die Wohnung aber auf keinen Fall aufgeben, ich hänge daran und finde in Wohlen nie wieder etwas so Günstiges.

Darf die Verwaltung mir das einfach so verbieten? Und was passiert, wenn ich Corinne trotzdem einziehen lasse? Ich muss mich bis Mitte August entscheiden und wäre um eine rasche Einschätzung froh.

Freundliche Grüsse
Esther Wälti
